exampleAnswers.title: Determining the Index of a Term in an Arithmetic Sequence

question.text: Given the arithmetic sequence $a_n=100-8n$ for $n\geq 1,$ the index of the term $-620$ is
question.explanation:
Using the formula for the $n$th term of an arithmetic sequence, we solve for the value of $n$ that gives $a_n=-620$, as follows: \begin{align*} a_n&= 100-8n \\[5pt] -620&= 100-8n\\[5pt] 8n&= 720 \\[5pt] n &=\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{90} \end{align*}

Therefore, $-620$ is the $90$th term of the sequence.

question.text: Given the arithmetic sequence $f(n)=2n-5$ for $n\geq 1,$what is the index of the term $41?$
question.explanation:
Using the formula for the $n$th term of an arithmetic sequence, we solve for the value of $n$ that gives $f(n)=41$, as follows:

\begin{align*} f(n)&= 2n-5 \\[3pt] 41&= 2n-5 \\[3pt] 46&= 2n \\[3pt] n&=23 \end{align*}

Therefore, $41$ is the $23$rd term of the sequence.

exampleAnswers.title: Determining the Index of a Term Given the Recursive Formula

question.text:
Given the arithmetic sequence 
\[
a_{n+1} = a_n - 6, \quad a_1 = 2,\quad n\geq 1, 
\]
the index of the term $-124$ is $n=$
question.explanation:
We will convert the recursive formula to an explicit formula and then solve for the value of $n$ such that $a_n=-124.$

The recursive rule for an arithmetic sequence takes the form \[ a_{n+1} = a_n +d. \]

In the given formula, we have $d=-6.$ We are also told that $a_1=2,$ so we can write the explicit formula as follows: \begin{align*} a_n &= a_1 + (n-1)d \\[5pt] &= 2 + (n-1)(-6) \\[5pt] &= 2- 6n + 6 \\[5pt] &= -6n+8 \end{align*}

Now, we solve for the value of $n$ such that $a_n=-124\mathbin{:}$ \begin{align*} a_n &= -6n+8 \\[5pt] -124 &= -6n+8 \\[5pt] -132 &= -6n \\[5pt] \dfrac{-132}{-6} &= n \\[5pt] 22 &=n \\[5pt] n &=\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{22} \end{align*}

Therefore, $-124$ is the $22$nd term of the sequence.

example.title: Determining the Index of a Term Given the Recursive Formula

question.text:
What is the index of the term $24$ for the arithmetic sequence below?

\[ a_{n+1} = a_n + 2, \quad a_1 = -8,\quad n\geq 1 \]
question.explanation:
We will convert the recursive formula to an explicit formula and then solve for the value of $n$ such that $a_n=24.$

The recursive rule for an arithmetic sequence takes the form \[ a_{n+1} = a_n +d. \]

In the given formula, we have $d=2.$ We are also told that $a_1=-8,$ so we can write the explicit formula as follows:

\begin{align*} a_n &= a_1 + (n-1)d \\[3pt] &= -8 + (n-1)(2) \\[3pt] &= -8+ 2n - 2 \\[3pt] &= 2n-10 \end{align*}

Now, we solve for the value of $n$ such that $a_n=24\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} a_n &= 2n-10 \\[3pt] 24 &= 2n-10 \\[3pt] 34 &= 2n \\[3pt] \dfrac{34}{2} &= n \\[3pt] 17 &= n \end{align*}

Therefore, $24$ is the $17$th term of the sequence.

exampleAnswers.title: Determining the Index of a Term Given Another Term and the Common Difference

question.text: If an arithmetic sequence has $f(15)= -4$ and common difference $d=-5$, find the value of $n$ such that $f(n) = -184.$
question.explanation:
Since $f(15)=-4$ is $14$ jumps after $f(1),$ we can determine the first term of the sequence: \begin{align*} f(15) &=f(1) + 14d \\[5pt] -4 &= f(1) + 14(-5) \\[5pt] -4 &= f(1) -70\\[5pt] 66 &= f(1) \end{align*}

So, the formula for the $n$th term is: \begin{align*} f(n) &= f(1) + (n-1)d \\[5pt] &= 66 + (n-1)(-5) \\[5pt] &= 66 -5n +5 \\[5pt] &= 71-5n \end{align*}

Now, we solve for the value of $n$ that gives $f(n)=-184,$ as follows: \begin{align*} f(n) &= 71-5n \\[5pt] -184 &= 71-5n \\[5pt] -255 &= -5n \\[5pt] n &= \dfrac{-255}{-5} \\[5pt] n &= \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{51} \end{align*}

Therefore, $-184$ is the $51$st term of the sequence.

example.title: Determining the Index of a Term Given Another Term and the Common Difference

question.text: Given an arithmetic sequence that has $f(11)= 78$ and common difference $d=4$, what is the index of the term $50?$
question.explanation:
Since $f(11)=78$ is $10$ jumps after $f(1),$ we can determine the first term of the sequence: \begin{align*} f(11) &= f(1) + 10d \\[5pt] 78 &= f(1) + 10(4) \\[5pt] 78 &= f(1) + 40 \\[5pt] 38 &= f(1) \end{align*}

So, the formula for the $n$th term is: \begin{align*} f(n) &= f(1) + (n-1)d \\[5pt] &= 38 + (n-1)(4) \\[5pt] &= 38 + 4n - 4 \\[5pt] &= 4n + 34 \end{align*}

Now, we solve for the value of $n$ that gives $f(n)=50,$ as follows: \begin{align*} f(n) &= 4n + 34 \\[5pt] 50 &= 4n + 34 \\[5pt] 16 &= 4n \\[5pt] \dfrac{16}{4} &= n \\[5pt] 4 &= n \end{align*}

Therefore, $50$ is the $4$th term of the sequence.

exampleAnswers.title: Determining the Index of a Term Given Two Terms

question.text: Given an arithmetic sequence that has $a_3=21$ and $a_{5} = 27,$ what is the index of the term $108?$
question.explanation:
To construct the formula for the sequence, we need to know the common difference $d$ and the first term $a_1.$

Since we are given $a_3=21$ and $a_5=27,$ we can find the common difference by dividing the total difference by the number of jumps:

\begin{align*} d &= \dfrac{a_5-a_3}{5-3} \\[5pt] &=\dfrac{27-21}{5-3} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{6}{2} \\[3pt] &= 3 \end{align*}

Now, since $a_3=21$ is $2$ jumps after $a_1,$ we can determine the first term of the sequence:

\begin{align*} a_3 &= a_1 + 2d \\[3pt] 21 &= a_1 +2(3) \\[3pt] 21 &= a_1 +6 \\[3pt] 15 &= a_1 \end{align*}

So, the formula for the $n$th term is:

\begin{align*} a_{n} &= a_1 + (n-1)d \\[3pt] &= 15 + (n-1)(3) \\[3pt] &= 15 + 3n - 3 \\[3pt] &= 3n + 12 \end{align*}

Now, we solve for the value of $n$ that gives $a_n=108,$ as follows:

\begin{align*} a_{n} &= 3n+12 \\[3pt] 108 &= 3n + 12 \\[3pt] 96 &= 3n \\[3pt] \dfrac{96}{3} &= n \\[5pt] 32 &= n \end{align*}

Therefore, $108$ is the $32$nd term of the sequence.

example.title: Determining the Index of a Term Given Two Terms

question.text: If an arithmetic sequence has $a_6=12$ and $a_{9} = 24$, find the value of $n$ such that $a_n = 132.$
question.explanation:
To construct the formula for the sequence, we need to know the common difference $d$ and the first term $a_1.$

Since we are given $a_6=12$ and $a_9=24,$ we can find the common difference by dividing the total difference by the number of jumps: \begin{align*} d &= \dfrac{a_9-a_6}{9-6} \\[5pt] &=\dfrac{24-12}{9-6} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{12}{3} \\[5pt] &= 4 \end{align*}

Now, since $a_6=12$ is $5$ jumps after $a_1,$ we can determine the first term of the sequence: \begin{align*} a_6 &= a_1 + 5d \\[5pt] 12 &= a_1+ 5(4) \\[5pt] 12 &= a_1+ 20 \\[5pt] -8 &= a_1 \end{align*}

So, the formula for the $n$th term is: \begin{align*} a_{n} &= a_1 + (n-1)d \\[3pt] &= -8 + (n-1)(4) \\[3pt] &= -8 +4n - 4 \\[3pt] &= 4n-12 \end{align*}

Now, we solve for the value of $n$ that gives $a_n=132,$ as follows: \begin{align*} a_{n} &= 4n-12 \\[5pt] 132 &= 4n-12 \\[5pt] 144 &= 4n \\[5pt] n &= \dfrac{144}{4} \\[5pt] n &= \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{36} \end{align*}

Therefore, $132$ is the $36$th term of the sequence.

example.title: Determining the Index of a Term Given Two Terms

question.text: Given an arithmetic sequence that has $a_2=5$ and $a_{5} = -4$, what is the index of the term $-73?$
question.explanation:
To construct the formula for the sequence, we need to know the common difference $d$ and the first term $a_1.$

Since we are given $a_2=5$ and $a_5=-4,$ we can find the common difference by dividing the total difference by the number of jumps:

\begin{align*} d &= \dfrac{a_5-a_2}{5-2} \\[5pt] &=\dfrac{-4-5}{5-2} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{-9}{3} \\[5pt] &= -3 \end{align*}

Now, since $a_2=5$ is $1$ jump after $a_1,$ we can determine the first term of the sequence:

\begin{align*} a_2 &= a_1 + d \\[3pt] 5 &= a_1 -3 \\[3pt] 8 &= a_1 \end{align*}

So, the formula for the $n$th term is:

\begin{align*} a_{n} &= a_1 + (n-1)d \\[3pt] &= 8 + (n-1)(-3) \\[3pt] &= 8 - 3n + 3 \\[3pt] &= 11-3n \end{align*}

Now, we solve for the value of $n$ that gives $a_n=-73,$ as follows:

\begin{align*} a_{n} &= 11 - 3n \\[3pt] -73 &= 11 - 3n \\[3pt] -84 &= -3n \\[3pt] \dfrac{-84}{-3} &= n \\[5pt] 28 &= n \end{align*}

Therefore, $-73$ is the $28$th term of the sequence.
